Tignish, PE C0B 2B0 Looking For CPA Employment Type Full Time Date Posted August 25, 2026 Salary Starting at $90K-$110K Submission Deadline unspecified Location Tignish JOB SUMMARY Reporting to the General Manager, the Corporate Controller will be accountable for the integrity of financial reporting, budgeting and forecasting, cash flow management, the day-to-day leadership of the finance team to support the organization’s long-term business planning. This position requires a strong understanding of accounting principles, financial regulations, and business operations, with a demonstrated commitment to maintaining the financial and ethical integrity of the organization. The Corporate Controller will ensure financial reporting is prepared in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and will maintain compliance with all applicable regulatory requirements and Canadian laws. Our Controller should be a strategic thinker who can translate financial data into actionable insights, drive operational efficiency, and strengthen internal controls and financial processes. OUR TEAM Within our team, we maintain a strong focus on performance, acknowledging and rewarding valuable contributions and recognizing talent. We value individuals that have a genuine passion for learning, a relentless drive for growth, and the vibrant energy needed to propel their career forward – all while being part of a dynamic team. JOB ACCOUNTABILITIES Job Accountabilities outline the responsibilities that an individual has for tasks, projects, and initiatives that they are assigned or involved in. In general, it focuses on being accountable for one’s actions, decisions, and performance, both in terms of achieving objectives and adhering to agreed-upon standards, guidelines, and expectations. General - Providing day to day support and guidance to the finance team - Managing financial operations, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, and payroll, ensuring and preparing accurate and timely financial reporting. - Oversee cash and banking activity, including daily bank monitoring, cheque signing, etc. - Collaborating with the executive team to develop and manage budgets, forecasts, and operational KPIs; analyze financial performance and implement cost-saving measures. - Providing year-end financial information to external accountants, to manage year end costs and achieve deliverables. - Maintain and strengthen internal controls and ensure finance processes are documented and consistently applied. - Oversee accounts receivable and collections, ensuring accurate reporting and timely follow-up, identifying and then implementing improvements to financial processes and systems to enhance operational efficiency and accuracy. - Provide payroll oversight, including processing and reviewing management and staff payrolls. - Support governance requirements, including attending board meetings and maintaining board minutes. - Ensuring compliance with all federal and provincial tax laws and regulations while working with external accountants on any complex tax issues. - Foster positive employee relations within the team through annual performance reviews and handling staff concerns appropriately and effectively. - Provide oversight for company IT (hardware/software/service vendors), ensuring continuity and appropriate access governance. Employee Relations/Team Engagement - Provide leadership to the Finance Team by offering training, coaching/mentoring, guidance, to support their personal development. - Identify challenges/problems and make quick decisions to resolve issues - resulting in errors identified prior to final financial reports being generated. - Develop and foster relationships with other departments encouraging continuous improvement through effective teamwork. - Effectively communicate expectations to employees with an emphasis on developing a high-performance finance team. - In conjunction with Human Resources assist in staff recruitment of new team members, including ensuring an effective and engaging onboarding process. - Foster an environment of open communications/interactions with all team members and other departments. - Performance Management: Identify team development opportunities, set realistic development plans, and provide opportunities for growth. Learning & Development - Actively participate in training provided to support personal development. - Identify personal professional training needs and opportunities for skill enhancement. - Foster a continuous improvement culture with a commitment to excellence - teamwork, finance practices, etc. – with an overall focus on accurate, timely reporting. - Provide guidance and support to employees in setting and achieving their own professional goals. - Stay informed about industry trends and best practices and share relevant information with team for teams’ overall development. QUALIFICATIONS Job Qualifications refer to the required experience, skills, and attributes a position requires. This section outlines the minimum Qualifications the company desires for this role, from leadership skills to education and training requirements. Leadership Skills - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, including written and verbal. - Act and speak in a professional manner by representing the company values and mission. - A strong ability to build collaborative relationships and effectively communicate financial insights across all levels of the organization. - Collaborator with strong listening, facilitation, and persuasion skills - Possesses strong analytical, problem-solving, interpersonal, and communication skills to foster positive employee relations. - Ability to prioritize work and motivate employees to achieve production results. - Understand people and operation lines, KPIs, budgets and cost of goods. - Demonstrated success in teamwork, change management and continuous improvement. - Dedicated to the goals and values of the company. - Adapts quickly to change in the work environment. - Demonstrated ability to develop and execute clear objectives. - Previous leadership and supervisory experience. - Ability to work with minimal supervision, taking initiative to achieve results. - Proactive, reliable, self-motivated, and committed to being a team player. - Capable of understanding and working with limited supervision; willingness to train other team members. - High tolerance for flexibility, change, and ambiguity. Education & Training - Bachelor’s Business Degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or related field. - Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. 5+ years post CPA designation experience preferred although equivalencies will be considered. - 3–7 years of experience managing people and processes within a team environment. - Strong computer skills with proficiency in MS Office: Excel, Word, and Outlook. - Advanced Excel skills preferred Other Requirements - Ability to provide a satisfactory Security Clearance Certificate (criminal record check) - Demonstrated knowledge of financial regulations, GAAP, and tax laws in Canada. - Commitment to being organized, with strong logistical and planning skills. - Experience in strategic planning and execution in a dynamic environment. KEY COMPETENCIES Key Competencies are skills and abilities that people need to perform the function of the job well (thinking, relating to others, communication, self-awareness, etc.). This section outlines the minimum Key Competencies the company desires for this role. Innovative Thinking - Thinking outside the box by creating new and better ways for the company to be successful. - Trust: Gains the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity. Team Builder - Collaborates: Builds partnerships and works collaboratively with others to meet company objectives. - Interpersonal Skills: Relates openly and comfortably with diverse groups of people. - Communication: Effectively conveys a clear understanding of the needs of the team/company. - Persuades: Uses effective techniques to gain the support and commitment of others. Performance Leader - Team Accountability: Holding self and others accountable to meet commitments. - Drives Results: Consistently achieving results, even under tough circumstances. - Takes Initiative: Taking on new opportunities and tough challenges with a sense of urgency, high energy, and enthusiasm. - Resourceful: Managing resources effectively and efficiently (product, people, etc.). - Self-Develop: Actively seeking ways to grow and be challenged using both formal and informal development opportunities. Managing the Work - Quality decisions: Making good and timely decisions that positively impact the company. - Optimize Processes: Knowing the most effective and efficient way to get things done with a focus on continuous improvement. LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES Leadership Competencies refer to a combination of knowledge, skills, and abilities a leader possesses, the expected leadership behavior of the company. These competencies include creating vision and strategy, mobilizing people, upholding integrity and respect, achieving results, promoting innovation, guiding change, and collaborating with partners and stakeholders. Innovative Thinking - Forward thinking mindset: Seeing future possibilities and translating them into workable strategies for the company. - Courageous: Comfortable stepping up to address difficult issues, saying what needs to be said while maintaining an engaged workforce. Performance Leader - Shares Vision/Purpose: Painting a clear picture for the team on what is to be accomplished. Managing the Work - Providing Direction: Delegating properly and removing obstacles to get work done by the team. - Planning: Prioritizing work to meet company plans and established timelines. About CookUnity Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, it has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Today, CookUnity delivers 50 million meals a year from the industry’s best chefs to homes all over the country. Fresh. Ready-to-eat. And crafted with the passion that nourishes body and soul. Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world. If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting. The Role CookUnity is looking for a Senior Data Analyst, B2B to own and scale analytics across our growing B2B business. Our B2B organization serves customers through multiple business models—including Corporate, Smart Fridge, and Healthcare—each with distinct go-to-market motions, customer journeys, and economics. You will build the analytics foundation that helps us understand how these businesses are performing, where our biggest growth opportunities are, and how we can scale them efficiently. You’ll partner closely with Sales, Partnerships, Sales Enablement, Marketing, Finance, and B2B leadership to connect the dots from pipeline generation and conversion through customer performance, retention, revenue, and profitability. This role is the connective tissue between the B2B business and CookUnity’s core Data team. Today, B2B analytics are spread across multiple tools—Salesforce, Tableau, Hex, and standalone dashboards—with no single owner consolidating them into a coherent, executive-ready view. You will be that owner. You’ll translate what B2B leadership needs to see into what the Data Engineering team needs to build, and ensure that every metric the business runs on is accurate, consistent, and available without manual effort. This is a highly visible role for someone who enjoys bringing structure to ambiguous business problems, building reliable metrics and reporting from the ground up, and translating data into recommendations that directly influence commercial decisions. What You’ll Do Own the analytics strategy for CookUnity’s B2B business, developing the reporting infrastructure, executive-ready dashboards, and analytical frameworks needed to understand and accelerate growth across Corporate, Smart Fridge, Healthcare, and emerging B2B opportunities (e.g., Airbnb, partnerships). Build an authoritative, single-source-of-truth view of B2B business health—clean data, executive-level visibility, one place leadership goes for the numbers. Partner with B2B leadership to translate business objectives into measurable KPIs and data models that connect the full commercial funnel—from lead generation and pipeline through conversion, activation, revenue, retention, and expansion. Partner with Sales, Partnerships, Sales Enablement, and Marketing to analyze pipeline health, conversion rates, sales velocity, win/loss patterns, deal velocity by stage, and other drivers of commercial productivity. Identify opportunities to improve how we acquire, prioritize, and grow B2B customers. Build the attribution layer that connects marketing spend to SQLs, pipeline created, and ARR won—by channel and by vertical. Partner with Finance and B2B leadership on forecasting and planning, translating pipeline and customer trends into forward-looking views of revenue and business performance, and helping explain gaps between plan and actuals. Own the data inputs for the Board-ready standard metric pack—including ARR bridge (opening → new → expansion → contraction → churn → closing), profitability trend, retention cohorts, stage-weighted pipeline, and efficiency metrics—per pod and consolidated. Develop a deep understanding of B2B business economics, including revenue, retention, expansion, order behavior, margins, and unit economics. Surface the segments, channels, ICPs (Ideal Customer Profiles), and customer profiles that create the greatest long-term value. Build LTV and CAC analysis at the B2B level to start, with increasing granularity by pod and ICP over time. Build the analytical frameworks needed to compare performance across B2B pods and business models, recognizing that success may look different across Corporate, Smart Fridge, and Healthcare while creating a common language and standard scorecard for leadership. Define what green/yellow/red looks like for each pod’s key metrics. Develop and maintain automated dashboards and reporting that give commercial teams and leadership timely visibility into pipeline, revenue, customer health, and key business drivers—reducing manual reporting and increasing confidence in the numbers. Consolidate today’s scattered reporting (Salesforce, Tableau, Hex, standalone tools) into a unified, reliable analytics layer. Go beyond reporting to diagnose what is driving performance. Proactively identify trends, risks, and opportunities and translate them into clear recommendations for Sales, Partnerships, Marketing, Finance, and B2B leadership. Own analyses like: retention by cohort with largest-account exclusion, pipeline movement waterfalls (added/advanced/slipped/lost), Healthcare funnel conversion (applications submitted → approved → contracting), and ICP-level performance tracking. Serve as the connective tissue between the B2B business and CookUnity’s core Data and Analytics Engineering teams. Translate B2B business requirements into data modeling and infrastructure needs. Partner with Analytics Engineering and Data Engineering to improve B2B data foundations—ensuring critical commercial and operational data (Salesforce ingestion, ad platform integrations, pricing logic, coupon attribution) is modeled consistently, accurately, and at the right level of granularity. Drive the B2B data alignment roadmap and ensure the Data team’s build priorities reflect the business’s most pressing analytical needs. Turn complex analyses into clear, compelling business stories. Present insights and recommendations to senior stakeholders—including Board-level presentations—in a way that makes the “so what” obvious and helps teams make faster, better decisions. Qualifications 5+ years of experience in analytics, ideally supporting B2B, enterprise sales, revenue operations, commercial strategy, or a similar go-to-market organization. Advanced proficiency in SQL, with the ability to independently explore, transform, validate, and analyze large and sometimes imperfect datasets. Strong understanding of B2B and commercial metrics, such as pipeline, funnel conversion, sales velocity, win rates, revenue, retention, expansion, account performance, and unit economics. Experience building dashboards, recurring business reporting, and executive-ready metric packs that become reliable sources of truth for commercial teams and leadership. Strong analytical problem-solving skills and the ability to take an ambiguous business question, structure it, identify the right data, and turn the analysis into a recommendation. Experience partnering with Sales, Finance, Marketing, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, or other commercial stakeholders, with an understanding of how analytics can influence both strategic and day-to-day decisions. Experience with business intelligence platforms such as Tableau, Looker, or equivalent. Strong communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex analyses into concise insights for both technical and non-technical audiences, including Board-level presentations. Excellent English, both written and spoken, given our U.S. presence and cross-functional collaboration. Comfortable operating with high autonomy in a fast-paced environment, balancing recurring reporting needs with deeper strategic analyses and proactively identifying where analytics can create value. Preferred Experience working with CRM and sales data, particularly Salesforce or similar platforms. Experience with revenue forecasting, sales capacity/productivity analysis, customer segmentation, or account-level economics. Experience analyzing businesses with multiple B2B go-to-market motions or customer segments (e.g., enterprise sales, self-serve/kiosk, marketplace, healthcare payer relationships). Familiarity with ETL, data warehousing, and data modeling concepts; experience with tools such as dbt and Snowflake is a plus. Experience working in a high-growth startup, marketplace, food-tech, or operationally complex business. Familiarity with connecting commercial data to financial and operational outcomes, rather than analyzing the sales funnel in isolation. Experience consolidating analytics across multiple disconnected tools and data sources into a unified reporting layer. Exposure to healthcare or regulated-industry sales cycles (RFPs, credentialing, payer contracting) is a plus. titulo: Sr. Software Engineer, AI / ML Inference Platform (Buenos Aires)
descripcion: Postúlate en Kit Empleo: kitempleo.com.ar/empleo/vusdm About Dialpad Dialpad is the AI platform for customer experience, built to resolve customer problems in real time across voice and digital. Our AI agents learn from your best human agents and improve with every interaction, helping organizations understand their customers, deliver better experiences, increase operational efficiencies, and build a lasting competitive advantage. Unlike legacy systems built to route and answer, or standalone agentic bot vendors built to deflect, Dialpad was built to resolve. Our AI agents and human agents operate on a single platform with shared context, allowing Agentic AI to resolve issues, advance deals, and eliminate busywork through automation while seamlessly handing conversations to humans when needed, with full context preserved. Market-leading brands, including Randstad, Motorola Solutions, Netflix, the San Diego Padres, the Colorado Rockies Baseball Club, and Cal Athletics, trust Dialpad. Dialpad is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, GV, ICONIQ Capital, and T-Mobile. Being a Dialer At Dialpad, AI isn’t just a feature; it’s how our teams do their best work every day. We put powerful AI tools in every employee’s hands so they can move faster, think bigger, and achieve more. We believe every conversation matters. And we’ve built the platform that turns those conversations into insight and action, for our customers and ourselves. We look for people who are intensely curious and hold themselves to a high bar. Our ambition is significant, and achieving it requires a team that operates at the highest level. We seek individuals who embody our core traits: Scrappy, Curious, Optimistic, Persistent, and Empathetic. Your role We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to build the shared AI / ML platform that takes Dialpad’s model-backed capabilities from training through production inference. The AI / ML Platform team builds and operates GPU training infrastructure, model evaluation and lifecycle tooling, and production inference systems running on NVIDIA GPUs in GCP. We provide the common engineering foundations that allow ASR, NLP, and other AI teams to train, evaluate, release, operate, and continually improve models at enterprise scale. Inference is an important center of gravity for this role: turning trained models into reliable, observable, efficient production services. The work is intentionally end-to-end, however, because production outcomes are shaped by decisions made throughout the model lifecycle. You will work across training clusters, model artifacts, evaluation and release workflows, serving runtimes, production operations, and feedback loops. You will also serve as a senior engineering partner to ASR and NLP scientists. You will help teams reason about reproducibility, evaluation, scalability, hardware and runtime constraints, latency, reliability, cost, and release safety while there is still time to influence the design. You will not be expected to conduct original ML research, but you must understand training, data, evaluation, and model behavior well enough to help translate scientific work into dependable enterprise ML systems. This is an implementation-heavy engineering role, not an operations support position. You will build systems directly, lead substantial technical work, and improve the shared practices by which Dialpad moves AI capabilities from experimentation into production. What you’ll do - Design, build, and improve shared platform capabilities spanning model training, evaluation, artifact management, release, production inference, and operational feedback. - Build and operate shared GPU training infrastructure that provides scientists with reliable, reproducible, and efficient environments for model development and experimentation. - Improve training-cluster scheduling, workload isolation, capacity management, storage, networking, observability, and accelerator utilization. - Develop production-serving pathways for low-latency, high-throughput, and highly available inference workloads. - Integrate and adapt model-training frameworks and inference runtimes to meet Dialpad’s requirements for automation, observability, security, and operational control. - Improve the performance and efficiency of GPU workloads by reasoning across compute, memory, storage, networking, batching, concurrency, and workload scheduling. - Partner with ASR and NLP scientists to translate evolving model capabilities into scalable production designs. - Counsel scientific teams on production concerns including reproducibility, evaluation coverage, artifact design, resource requirements, serving feasibility, failure modes, and quality–performance trade-offs. - Improve how models and related artifacts are versioned, traced, validated, compared, promoted, deployed, and rolled back across environments. - Enable safe releases through representative evaluation, automated quality and performance checks, shadow traffic, staged rollouts, candidate-versus-incumbent comparisons, and fast rollback. - Build benchmarking and evaluation infrastructure that measures model quality alongside latency, throughput, saturation behavior, reliability, resource utilization, and cost. - Strengthen telemetry, structured logging, tracing, dashboards, alerting, and diagnostic tooling across training and production environments. - Use performance data, incidents, developer feedback, and production model behavior to identify and deliver high-value improvements across the AI lifecycle. - Reduce recurring manual work by building self-service workflows, clear interfaces, and practical standards that other AI teams can adopt. - Lead technical projects from design through production operation, contribute to architectural decisions, and mentor other engineers. Skills you’ll bring - Production engineering experience: Seven or more years of professional software engineering experience, with demonstrated ownership of backend, infrastructure, distributed, or ML platform systems in production. - ML systems experience: Experience building or operating systems that support model training, model inference, or the lifecycle connecting them. - Strong software fundamentals: Proficiency in Python, Go, or another backend-oriented language, with a record of producing maintainable production software and well-designed interfaces. - Cloud and Kubernetes fluency: Hands-on experience with Linux, containers, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, deployment automation, and production operations. - Accelerated-computing knowledge: Experience operating GPU workloads and reasoning about utilization, memory, storage, networking, scheduling, and workload performance. - Training familiarity: Working knowledge of modern model-training workflows, including datasets, experiments, distributed execution, checkpoints, reproducibility, and model artifacts. - Applied data-science fluency: An understanding of dataset quality, evaluation design, experimental validity, error analysis, model-quality metrics, and production model behavior sufficient to collaborate effectively with applied scientists. - Systems and performance judgment: The ability to find bottlenecks across system boundaries and make reasoned trade-offs among model quality, latency, throughput, reliability, capacity, and cost. - Operational judgment: A strong instinct for observability, repeatability, release safety, failure containment, rollback, and whole-system resilience. - Technical leadership: The ability to independently lead ambiguous projects, communicate clearly across disciplines, mentor engineers, and influence decisions through sound technical reasoning. Particularly relevant experience You do not need experience with every technology or domain listed below. Experience in several of these areas would be especially valuable: - ASR, speech processing, NLP, large language models, or other production model-backed systems. - GPU-based or distributed model training. - Model-serving runtimes such as vLLM, Triton, TGI, or comparable systems. - Model-development frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX. - Kubernetes-based GPU scheduling and workload management. - GCP infrastructure, particularly GKE and related storage, networking, and observability services. - Experiment tracking, model evaluation, artifact registries, or production model monitoring. - Building internal platforms for scientific and engineering users. How we work We treat an enterprise ML capability as more than a trained model. It includes the data and evaluation evidence behind the model; the infrastructure used to train it; the artifact and release process; the runtime and hardware on which it operates; and the telemetry, safeguards, and feedback loops required to operate and improve it. We favor practical, incremental improvements over unnecessary platform expansion. We build shared capabilities where they remove recurring friction, improve reliability, or create meaningful leverage while preserving the flexibility scientists need to explore and iterate. Success in this role means that scientists can move from an idea to a production-ready capability with less manual work and stronger evidence—and that deployed models become easier to understand, operate, and improve over time. Why Join Dialpad - Work at the center of the AI transformation in business communications - Build and ship agentic AI products that are redefining how companies operate - Join a team where AI amplifies every employee’s impact - Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and real opportunities for growth We believe in investing in our people. Dialpad offers competitive benefits and perks, cutting-edge AI tools, and a robust training program that help you reach your full potential. We have designed our offices to be inclusive, offering a vibrant environment to cultivate collaboration and connection. Our exceptional culture, repeatedly recognized as a Great Place to Work, ensures that every employee feels valued and empowered to contribute to our collective success. Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role and possess the fundamental traits, drive, and strong ambition we seek, but your experience doesn’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply. Dialpad is an equal-opportunity employer. We are dedicated to creating a community of inclusion and an environment free from discrimination or harassment. descripcion: Why Work at Banner? For over 50 years, Banner Engineering has been at the forefront of industrial automation. We offer products and solutions including award-winning sensors, wireless solutions, machine safety, indication and LED lighting. From Fortune 500 leaders to innovative startups, Banner's award-winning products and solutions are helping companies around the world increase efficiency, reduce costs, safeguard equipment, and protect personnel. Our commitment to innovation shows through a continuous, market-driven evolution of products and technology. With engineers employed in nearly every major department, engineering is in our DNA. Banner is a rapidly growing company that offers many personal development opportunities, an excellent benefits package, and a collaborative team of employees who are passionate about what they do. Position Summary The Senior Supply Chain Planner will play a critical role in advancing Banner’s inventory planning capability and stocking program strategy. This role will support and drive the processes, analytics, and cross-functional decision-making needed to improve in-stock levels at Banner and across distributor channels while balancing customer service, working capital, operational constraints, and product lifecycle priorities. The position will partner closely with Operations, Commercial, Product Management, Supply Chain, and regional teams to translate demand signals, stocking policies, service-level expectations, and product-family strategies into actionable inventory plans. The role will help define which products should be stocked, where inventory should be positioned, how stocking levels should be maintained, and how exceptions should be surfaced for decision-making. This position reports to Demand Planning Manager. This role requires working onsite at our Brooklyn Park, MN office five days a week. What You’ll Be Doing This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working Collaboratively and Individually, staying on top of tasks, and making a meaningful impact across teams and projects. Below are some key responsibilities of the role. Key Responsibilities Support the development and execution of Banner’s stocking program strategy, including P/S/N stocking recommendations, min/max logic, demand segmentation, and service-level targets. Analyze inventory availability, forecast inputs, demand behavior, backlog, open sales orders, lead times, and distributor requirements to identify gaps in in-stock performance. Partner with Product Management and Commercial teams to align stocking decisions with product-family strategy, lifecycle stage, customer promise, distributor expectations, and revenue priorities. Work with Operations and Supply Chain teams to translate stocking strategy into executable replenishment, production, and material plans. Develop reporting and dashboards to monitor in-stock levels, inventory health, service levels, forecast quality, slow-moving inventory, excess exposure, and stocking-policy effectiveness. Identify root causes of stockouts, inventory imbalances, past-due backlog, slow-moving inventory, and unmanaged stocking drift; recommend corrective actions and process improvements. Support monthly forecast and inventory reviews, product-family health reviews, and cross-functional stocking governance forums. Evaluate demand patterns using segmentation methods such as ABC/XYZ, runners/repeaters/strangers, lifecycle stage, customer concentration, and revenue contribution. Recommend stocking policy updates, safety stock assumptions, replenishment parameters, and exception-handling rules based on data, business priorities, and operational feasibility. Coordinate with distributor-facing and regional teams to understand channel inventory needs, availability gaps, lead-time expectations, and communication requirements. Help build standard work, planning tools, and repeatable processes that improve inventory decision quality and reduce reliance on ad hoc analysis. Escalate material stocking risks, service-level tradeoffs, or inventory exposure issues with clear options, financial impact, and recommended next steps. What You Bring To The Table To perform this job successfully, you must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily, and regular attendance is required. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to perform this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to support individuals with disabilities. Required Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Business, Finance, Engineering, Data Analytics, or a related field. 5+ years of experience in demand planning, inventory planning, supply planning, operations analytics, commercial operations, or a related manufacturing environment. Strong analytical capability with experience translating large datasets into business insights, recommendations, and action plans. Experience with inventory management concepts including safety stock, min/max, service levels, forecast accuracy, lifecycle planning, SKU segmentation, and excess/obsolete inventory. Working knowledge of ERP, MRP, forecasting, planning, or inventory optimization systems; experience with Oracle, GAINS, Qlik, Power BI, Excel, or similar tools preferred. Ability to work cross-functionally with Operations, Supply Chain, Product Management, Sales, Finance, Customer Care, and regional teams. Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain analytical findings, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations to both technical and business audiences. Demonstrated ability to manage ambiguity, structure problems, drive follow-up, and influence decisions without direct authority. Preferred Qualifications Experience in industrial manufacturing, automation, electronics, or distribution-supported business models. Familiarity with make-to-stock, configure-to-order, build-to-order, and engineer-to-order fulfillment models. Experience supporting SIOP, product lifecycle management, stocking strategy, distributor inventory programs, or product-family business reviews. Advanced Excel, data visualization, SQL, Power BI, Qlik, or similar analytics skills. APICS/ASCM CPIM, CSCP, or related supply chain certification preferred. Success Measures Improved in-stock levels for priority and stocked items at Banner and key distributor locations. Improved accuracy and discipline of stocking parameters, including P/S/N status, min/max levels, and replenishment assumptions. Better visibility to inventory gaps, stockout drivers, slow-moving inventory, and service-level tradeoffs. Clearer linkage between product-family strategy, commercial demand signals, and executable supply plans. Reduction in unmanaged inventory drift, excess exposure, and recurring planning exceptions. Repeatable reporting cadence and governance process for inventory and stocking decisions. The role involves demand forecasting, inventory management, data analysis, and collaboration with Customer Service, Supply Chain, external customers, and other departments to support smooth production processes, improve electronic communication, and contribute to the Order to Cash process in a LEAN environment. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, eager to learn, and capable of working in a fast-paced environment. This position does not have direct reports. Responsibilities Customer Forecast Management: Receive, review, and analyze customer forecasts to identify demand trends, risks, requirement changes, and forecast variability. S&OP Support: Participate in the Sales & Operations Planning process for assigned sites by aligning customer demand, production capacity, material availability, inventory strategies, service goals, cost objectives, and operational requirements. Position Summary The Senior Business Intelligence Developer leads the design, development, and delivery of enterprise BI solutions that support strategic business objectives and data-driven decision making. This role manages BI projects from initiation through implementation, collaborates with Data Engineers to optimize data pipelines and ETL processes, and develops complex data models that transform structured and unstructured data into meaningful insights. Working closely with business stakeholders, Data Governance teams, and technical partners, the Senior BI Developer translates analytical findings into actionable recommendations, ensures compliance with data governance and security standards, and drives continuous improvement of BI platforms and infrastructure. The role also provides technical leadership, mentors team members on BI best practices, and helps shape the organization's Business Intelligence strategy to maximize business value. This position belongs to a family of jobs with increasing responsibility, competency, and skill level. Actual position title and pay grade will be based on the selected candidate’s experience and qualifications. Key Responsibilities Leads Business Intelligence projects from initiation to completion. Collaborates with Data Engineers to optimize data pipelines and ETL processes. Executes data extraction from diverse sources, including structured and unstructured data. Collaborates cross-functionally to drive business decisions using Business Intelligence. Collaborates with Data Governance teams to ensure data compliance and security. Mentors and guides less experienced professionals in Business Intelligence best practices. Develops and maintains complex data models to extract meaningful business insights. Recommends improvements to existing Business Intelligence infrastructure. Interprets data findings and translates them into actionable business strategies. Oversees the integration of Business Intelligence tools with other business systems. Drives Business Intelligence strategies aligned with the company's business goals. Education and Experience Bachelor’s Degree in Information Technology, related field or equivalent experience. 5+ years of relevant Business Intelligence Developer experience required. SQL: Proficient in writing table joins, aggregation, indexes, views, and nested queries Power BI: Proficient in Power Query transformations, writing measures in DAX, defining STAR schema models, creating user-friendly business visualizations using AI copilots to author and review code, and using Git to version control Power BI code. Skills Analytical Thinking - Strong problem-solving skills to identify architectural challenges, analyze requirements, evaluate options, and propose effective solutions. Dashboard Reporting – The ability to access information from databases, forms, and other sources, and prepare reports according to requirements. Data Analysis – The process of measuring and managing organizational data, identifying methodological best practices, and conducting statistical analyses. Data Interpretations – Data interpretation involves analyzing and extracting meaningful insights from raw data, transforming it into a comprehensible and actionable format. It often requires the application of statistical methods, visualization techniques, and domain knowledge to derive informed conclusions and make data-driven decisions. Data Mining – Data mining is sorting through data to identify patterns and establish relationships. Data mining parameters include: Association - looking for patterns where one event is connected to another event Sequence or path analysis - looking for patterns where one event leads to another later event Classification - looking for new patterns [May result in a change in the way the data is organized but that's ok] Clustering - finding and visually documenting groups of facts not previously known Forecasting - discovering patterns in data that can lead to reasonable predictions about the future Data mining techniques are used in mathematics, cybernetics, and genetics. Web mining, a type of data mining used in customer relationship management [CRM], takes advantage of the huge amount of information gathered by a Web site to look for patterns in user behavior. Data Preparation – Data preparation, data wrangling, also known as data munging, refers to the process of cleaning, structuring, and transforming raw data into a suitable format for analysis or other purposes. It involves tasks such as handling missing values, standardizing formats, and merging datasets to ensure data quality and usability. Data Privacy – Ability to understand and implement practices that ensure the protection and confidential handling of personal and sensitive information. This includes knowledge of relevant laws and regulations (such as GDPR or HIPAA), the ability to design and enforce policies that safeguard data, and the skills to manage data access rights and consent protocols. Data Quality Management – Strong understanding of data quality dimensions, methodologies, and best practices to establish and maintain data quality standards and processes. Data Visualization – Skill in designing and creating compelling visualizations and data stories that effectively communicate insights and facilitate decision-making. Predictive Analytics – Augmented Analytics refers to the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies to enhance data preparation, insight generation, and decision-making within analytics processes. It automates data analysis, identifies patterns, and provides natural language processing interfaces to empower non-technical users with actionable insights, making the analytics process more accessible and efficient. Structured Query Language (SQL) – SQL (Structured Query Language) is a standardized programming language designed for managing and manipulating relational databases. It enables users to interact with databases by defining, querying, updating, and managing data stored in a relational database management system (RDBMS). SQL allows users to perform various operations such as retrieving data, inserting new records, updating existing records, and deleting records, as well as creating and modifying database structures like tables, indexes, views, and stored procedures. Job Overview The Junior Software Engineer provides hands-on development and engineering support to the Splunk Engineering and Maintenance team supporting government agencies. Working under the direction of senior Data, Platform, and Detection Engineers, this role contributes across the full breadth of the SIEM environment: onboarding and normalizing data sources, maintaining platform infrastructure and configurations, developing searches, dashboards, and content, and automating recurring engineering tasks through scripting and code. This is an entry-level, growth-oriented position for an engineer with a software development or cybersecurity foundation who is expected to build depth in Splunk and security operations over time. The Junior Software Engineer collaborates with senior engineers, security analysts, and agency stakeholders, and follows established code review, testing, and change management practices. Essential Functions Software Development and Automation. Write, test, and maintain scripts and small applications (Python, Bash, PowerShell) that automate recurring Splunk engineering, maintenance, and reporting tasks. Use version control, peer code review, and established branching and deployment practices for all code and configuration changes. Data Engineering Support. Assist with onboarding new log sources, including configuration of inputs, forwarders, parsing rules (props and transforms), source types, and index assignment. Support data quality efforts by validating field extractions, timestamps, event breaking, and Common Information Model (CIM) normalization under senior engineer guidance. Platform Engineering and Maintenance. Support routine maintenance of the Splunk environment, including indexers, search heads, forwarders, deployment servers, and app and patch deployments. Monitor platform health, license usage, ingest volume, and search performance; identify anomalies and assist senior engineers with troubleshooting and remediation. Content Development. Develop and maintain SPL searches, reports, dashboards, and alerts that support security, operational, and mission use cases. Assist Detection Engineers with building, testing, documenting, and deploying detection content through established review and release workflows. Testing, Documentation, and Quality. Test changes in development and test environments prior to production deployment and validate results against expected outcomes. Maintain technical documentation, configuration standards, runbooks, and knowledge articles for the work performed. Operational and Customer Support. Respond to assigned tickets and user requests for Splunk access, search assistance, data questions, and minor configuration changes. Provide data and platform context in support of incident response, audits, and after-action activities as directed. Collaboration and Professional Development. Participate in stand-ups, sprint planning, code reviews, and change management processes with the Splunk Engineering and Maintenance team. Work with senior engineers to translate requirements into technical tasks, and progress toward Splunk certification and technical specialization. Qualifications US Citizen with an active Top Secret Security Clearance. Bachelor's degree in computer science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field; equivalent technical training, certifications, or demonstrable experience will be considered. 0-2 years of professional software development, IT engineering, or cybersecurity experience; internship, co-op, apprenticeship, or substantial project work is applicable. Working proficiency in at least one programming or scripting language such as Python, Bash, PowerShell, Java, Go, or JavaScript. Comfort operating in a Linux command-line environment and a foundational understanding of system administration concepts. Familiarity with version control (Git) and standard development workflows including branching, pull requests, and code review. Ability to work with structured and semi-structured data formats such as JSON, XML, CSV, YAML, and syslog, including basic use of regular expressions. Foundational understanding of networking and logging concepts (TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP, authentication events) and how security-relevant events are generated across endpoint, network, and cloud. Foundational cybersecurity knowledge, including core security principles, common attack patterns, and the role of a SIEM in security operations. Willingness and demonstrated ability to learn Splunk and the Splunk Search Processing Language (SPL) quickly. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work for other engineers and non-technical stakeholders. Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to take direction and follow established engineering processes. Ability to obtain and maintain the clearance and suitability requirements for the contract. Preferred Hands-on exposure to Splunk (SPL, dashboards, universal forwarders, apps) or another SIEM such as Elastic, Microsoft Sentinel, QRadar, or Google SecOps. Splunk Core Certified User or Splunk Core Certified Power User, or willingness to obtain within the first year. CompTIA Security+, Network+, or a comparable industry certification. Experience with REST APIs, data parsing and normalization, and data pipeline concepts. Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and their native logging services. The Principal NLP Scientist is a senior technical leader responsible for designing, researching, and improving advanced Natural Language Processing and Large Language Model capabilities for production business systems. This role combines applied research, hands-on model development, technical architecture, and practical product impact. The Principal NLP Scientist will lead the design of NLP solutions for named entity recognition, text classification, text generation, semantic search, information extraction, and other language-driven automation use cases. This is not only a research role. The focus is to take modern NLP and LLM technologies and make them reliable, measurable, maintainable, and useful inside real production workflows. Assigned Product Group - Product Group | NLP / AI Automation - Stream | Software Engineering / AI & Machine Learning - Role Type | Principal-level individual contributor / technical leader The Principal NLP Scientist will work closely with software engineers, data engineers, product managers, analysts, and data annotation teams to define, build, evaluate, and continuously improve NLP models and language-based automation systems. Product Group Focus Areas The NLP product group is responsible for building and improving systems related to: - Named entity recognition and structured data extraction - Text classification and categorization - Text generation and language-based automation - Large Language Model evaluation, adaptation, and integration - Retrieval-augmented generation and semantic search - Knowledge graph and GraphRAG-based approaches for connecting structured business data, unstructured text, and entity relationships in AI assistant workflows - Data preparation, annotation strategy, and labeling quality - Model evaluation, monitoring, and production performance - Applied NLP research and prototype development - Integration of NLP models into internal business applications Insight on Your Impact In this role, you will influence how the company uses modern NLP and LLM technologies across internal platforms and operational workflows. You will define technical direction for NLP systems, evaluate new approaches, design experiments, create prototypes, and help move successful models into production. Your work will directly affect automation quality, data processing accuracy, operational efficiency, and the long-term AI capabilities of the company. The Global Supply Chain Process & Systems Manager is responsible for driving standardization, efficiency, and excellence across the company’s global supply chain organization. The Day To Day Business Process Leadership - Define, harmonize, and optimize end‑to‑end supply chain processes globally (Plan, Source, Procure, Deliver, Maintain & Sustain). - Establish global process governance and standards to ensure consistency across regions and business units (aligning with IMS and MOS standards, audit, and governance frameworks). - Identify and implement process improvements to reduce inefficiencies, duplications, and operational risks to ensure a robust and sustainable framework across all SSR operating mine sites. Systems Ownership (SAP & SCM Tools) - Serve as global process owner for SAP Supply Chain modules (MM, WM/EWM, PP, FICO, etc.) and related SCM systems (MIDAS, IDP). - Partner with IT to ensure system enhancements align with business requirements. - Drive adoption of digital solutions and advanced analytics within the supply chain function. Change Management & Training - Lead global training initiatives to strengthen user adoption of processes and systems. - Act as a change champion to embed a culture of process discipline and data‑driven decision‑making. Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement - Partner with Operations, Maintenance, Asset Management, and Finance to ensure supply chain systems and data support business needs. - Represent Supply Chain in global system projects, upgrades, and SAP S/4HANA transformation initiatives. Deeply understand the business and build a comprehensive map of KPIs, drivers, and relationships across the customer lifecycle. Quickly investigate ambiguous business problems and turn them into structured analytical questions. Raise the quality, speed, and impact of analytical work across the team. Ensure that insights are not just descriptive but lead to clear actions, experiments, and measurable outcomes. Strong understanding of product metrics, funnels, cohorts, retention, experimentation, and behavioral analytics. Ability to move beyond reporting and understand why metrics move and what actions can influence them. Strong business acumen and curiosity—you enjoy getting deep into how the business actually works. Ability to work effectively with very different audiences, from technical teams to Product, Operations, and senior leadership. At ExtraHop, we’re on a mission to protect and empower the connected enterprise. We reveal what is happening in the very infrastructure that sustains businesses, lives, and communities, and ensure the integrity of networks, data, systems, and processes. Organizations rely on ExtraHop to provide visibility into the cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and network performance issues that evade their existing security and IT tools. Position Summary ExtraHop is at the forefront of cybersecurity innovation, delivering Network Detection and Response (NDR) solutions that help organizations detect, investigate, and respond to cyber threats in real time. Join ExtraHop as a Senior Data Scientist and help advance the machine learning and artificial intelligence capabilities that power our products. You will analyze large-scale network telemetry, develop and evaluate methods for identifying malicious behavior, and improve the accuracy and efficacy of ExtraHop’s threat detection capabilities. This is an applied data science role for someone who enjoys solving ambiguous, high-impact problems using statistical analysis, experimentation, and machine learning. You will work closely with other data scientists, threat researchers, and software engineers to translate research into reliable product capabilities, and play a key role in contributing to the improvement of the RevealX platform. Key Responsibilities Analyze large-scale network telemetry to identify behavioral patterns, anomalies, and signals associated with malicious activity. Design, develop, and refine machine learning and AI-based methods that support ExtraHop’s products. Develop evaluation methods appropriate for cybersecurity data, including highly imbalanced datasets, incomplete labels, rare events, and changing attacker and network behavior. Conduct exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, model development, and error analysis using complex, high-volume datasets. Research emerging machine learning and AI techniques, relevant cybersecurity developments, and assess their applicability to ExtraHop’s products. Establish metrics and monitoring strategies for measuring model and detector performance over time. Communicate findings, limitations, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly to technical stakeholders and product leaders. Provide technical leadership and mentorship to other data scientists through code reviews, design discussions, technical strategy, and contributions to the team’s analytical and engineering standards. Document methodologies, experiments, model behavior, and evaluation results. Write clean, maintainable, and well-tested production-quality code. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, or another quantitative discipline, or equivalent practical experience. 7+ years of professional experience in data science, including developing and evaluating machine learning models for real-world use cases, defining meaningful success metrics, and conducting rigorous offline and online evaluations. Strong foundation in statistics, experimental design, machine learning, and model evaluation. Experience working with incomplete, noisy, or highly imbalanced data; performing detailed error analysis; and identifying the causes of false positives and false negatives. Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, experience with common data science and machine learning libraries, and the ability to write maintainable, tested, and reviewable code. Experience collaborating with software engineers to integrate data science methods into production systems. Strong problem-solving skills, intellectual curiosity, and a track record of independently owning complex technical work. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical findings, uncertainty, and tradeoffs to varied audiences. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, or another quantitative discipline. Experience applying data science or machine learning to cybersecurity, fraud detection, abuse detection, anomaly detection, or another adversarial domain. Familiarity with Network Detection and Response, network protocols, threat detection, or incident investigation. Experience with time-series analysis, anomaly detection, actuarial modeling, clustering, graph analytics, or unsupervised and semi-supervised learning. Experience evaluating models in domains where positive examples are rare, labels are incomplete, and the underlying behavior changes over time. Experience with generative AI, large language models, agentic systems, or other emerging AI techniques. Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP. descripcion: Principal AI Research Scientist: Designing Multi-Scale Intelligence for the Energy Transition Remote • Full-time • Three-year grant-funded term (renewable) Link to application: https://noteforms.com/forms/principal-ai-research-scientist-application-tgtkdo Ready to help shape the next frontier of AI by designing intelligent systems that reason across nested scales—from buildings to cities to nations—to accelerate the global energy transition. Open Earth Foundation (OEF) is a non-profit research and development organization building open digital infrastructure for planetary stewardship. We develop open digital infrastructure, AI systems, and data platforms that strengthen multi-stakeholder coordination and accelerate environmental protection, climate action, and Earth-system resilience. We’re a diverse, global team working remotely and collaborating with partners worldwide to make real change possible. With strong funding and a powerhouse team of innovators, we’re ready to tackle big challenges for a resilient Earth for generations to come and we need the planet’s brightest minds to help solve them! Your mission, should you choose to accept it: As the Principal AI Research Scientist for NEST at Open Earth Foundation, you will define the AI research architecture behind a new generation of intelligent systems for multi-scale energy-transition planning. You will set the research agenda, design the nested-agent and reasoning architectures that underpin the programme, and help shape its long-term scientific vision. NEST (Nested Energy System Transitions) is a three-year research programme funded by Schmidt Sciences through the Decarbonization and Energy Virtual Institute (DEVI) initiative. The programme is developing AI-agent architectures that connect existing energy models across nested spatial, temporal, and organizational scales, from buildings and cities to national systems, and from near-term operations to multi-decadal planning. The goal is to produce coherent energy-transition pathways by advancing both the intelligent systems and agentic research processes needed for cross-scale reasoning and model coupling. This is an architectural research role, not a production engineering role. You will design and validate new approaches, working closely with consortium Principal Investigators, Active Inference Scientists, and the Full-Stack AI Engineers who translate promising directions into robust systems. Success in this role could redefine how intelligent systems reason across interacting models, disciplines, and scales—well beyond climate and energy applications. This position is fully remote and international as our organization works across different time zones. This position is fully remote and international, full-time, and grant-funded for a three-year term with the possibility of renewal. Regular overlap with Central European and U.S. Pacific working hours required. Opportunities to participate in occasional in-person team gatherings. Priority will be given to applications submitted by August 14th. The following requirements describe our ideal candidate. If you don't meet some of the requirements, you're encouraged to apply anyway. Let us know if there is something missing and how we can work together to make it up. Essential Functions and Specific Duties: Set the AI research direction: Define and drive NEST’s agenda for agentic, probabilistic, and multi-scale intelligence across coupled models. Design nested intelligence: Co-design nested agents, advanced agent architectures, and the agentic research processes that make cross-scale coupling possible. Create coherent representations: Explore hierarchical agents, latent-state representations, world models, and uncertainty-aware methods that remain consistent across spatial, temporal, and organizational scales. Prototype and validate: Turn original research ideas into working prototypes and research instruments through hands-on experimentation and rapid iteration. Bridge research and production: Hand promising designs and coupling strategies to the Lead Full-Stack AI Engineer to harden into the production platform. Align with inference science: Partner with the Active Inference Scientist so the intelligence architecture and Bayesian inference layer—including factor graphs, message passing, and convergence—fit together. Set the scientific bar: Define standards for reproducibility, validation, posterior predictive checks, and comparison with established model couplings and benchmarks. Publish and represent the work: Shape NEST’s long-term scientific vision and communicate the research through publications, presentations, and external collaborations. Other: Actively participate in team building and culture-development activities at Open Earth Foundation. Contribute to an open, collaborative research culture grounded in rigor, curiosity, and shared purpose. Qualifications: PhD advancing the AI/ML field with a track record of original contributions in architectures, reasoning frameworks, or research methodologies—not only applications of existing models. Deep expertise in probabilistic reasoning, Bayesian methods, machine learning, or related approaches for uncertainty-aware AI systems. A record of turning ambitious ideas into rigorous research and impactful outcomes. Hands-on ability to translate research into working prototypes through experimentation and rapid iteration. Deep technical understanding of modern AI systems and agentic architectures. A deep commitment to safe, beneficial AI and using AI for the good of humanity. Strong written and verbal English communication skills. Strong Preference: Interest in world models, scientific AI, structured reasoning systems, or multi-scale reasoning LLM agent architectures, nested or multi-agent design, and tool-use frameworks Familiarity with energy systems, climate science, or scientific computing Nice to Have: Multi-model simulation, co-simulation, or model-coupling frameworks Active Inference, probabilistic programming, message-passing inference, or factor graphs Contributions to open-source scientific software Geospatial data processing, including GeoJSON, H3, or PostGIS Interpersonal Skills: Ability to collaborate across AI research, engineering, energy modelling, Bayesian inference, and programme leadership Ability to explain complex research choices clearly to technical and interdisciplinary audiences Comfort working independently in a distributed, international research team Other Qualities: Dedication to fighting climate change Intellectual courage, curiosity, and scientific rigor Focus on real-world impact and open research Interest in nonprofit, mission-driven work Compensation and Benefits: This full-time position offers compensation of $80,000–$130,000/ year (USD), commensurate with experience and location and paid in USD. A defining role at the frontier of agentic and multi-scale AI, applied to global environmental challenges. Unlimited paid time off, paid holidays, and paid sick leave. Backblaze is the object storage leader in the open cloud movement, fueling customer success with cloud storage built purposefully to unlock budgets, unburden administrators, and unleash innovators. Together with our partners, we’re helping customers break free from the restrictive, overpriced legacy solutions that hold them back, and blaze forward with the full power of the open cloud in their hands. Founded in 2007, we scaled the business with less than $3 million in outside funding until 2021, when we did a traditional IPO on the Nasdaq stock exchange. Today, Backblaze generates over $100m in revenue and is the leading specialized storage cloud - managing over three billion gigabytes of data storage for 500K+ customers in 175+ countries, including businesses, developers, IT professionals, and individuals. But while there is a lot to celebrate in our past, there is almost as much opportunity ahead of us. We are seeking an AI Workflow Engineer ! About The Role Backblaze is running a company-wide AI transformation program, and this role is where strategy becomes something you can actually use. As AI Workflow Engineer, you will be the hands-on builder inside the AI Program Office - embedded alongside the Director, AI Enablement, and deployed into non-GTM, non-Engineering business teams to prototype, build, and ship AI-powered workflow solutions that make a measurable difference in how work gets done. This is not a research role or a strategy role. You will spend your time building: prompt architectures, automation flows, lightweight agents, API integrations, and demos that help a business team see - concretely - what AI can do for them. You will move across functions, which means you need to understand how businesses actually operate. The ideal background is someone who started in a business-facing role - finance, operations, marketing, customer success, HR - and developed serious hands-on AI and automation skills on top of that foundation. You will work closely with the Director, AI Enablement, who owns the program management and delivery layer. Your job is to make their scoped solutions real - fast, iteratively, and with enough rigor that what you build can go to production. What You Will Do Build and Ship AI Workflow Solutions Take scoped use cases from the Director, AI Enablement and build working solutions: prompt layers, automation flows, lightweight agents, RAG implementations, and API integrations that connect AI tools to the systems business teams already use Build working prototypes quickly - the goal is to show a team what is possible in days, not weeks, then refine based on what actually lands Translate a documented workflow assessment into a technical design, select the right tools for the job, and own the build through to a deployable solution Maintain solution documentation that is clear enough for handoff, iteration, and audit - not just for engineers, but for the business owner who will live with it Embed in Business Teams Spend time inside the functions you are building for - Finance, HR, Legal, Marketing Ops, Customer Success, and others - understanding how the work actually flows before you redesign it Run working sessions with team members to map current-state workflows, surface friction points, and identify where AI creates real leverage versus where it creates noise Build credibility with non-technical stakeholders by showing them working solutions, not decks - and by being honest about what will and will not work Support user acceptance testing and early adoption, troubleshooting issues close to launch and iterating based on real usage Support the AI Program Office Build demos and proof-of-concepts that help the Director, AI Enablement make the case for a use case - or disqualify it early before resources are committed Contribute to vendor and tool evaluations with a builder's perspective: not just whether a tool claims to do something, but whether it actually works in the context of a specific workflow Feed learnings from the build process back into the program - what worked, what did not, what should be standardized across functions Work on tactical quick wins and longer-horizon strategic builds at the same time, switching contexts across active use cases as priorities shift What Success Looks Like (First 90 Days) You have completed at least one workflow assessment alongside the Director and produced a working prototype from it At least one solution you built is in active use by a business team, with a named owner and feedback loop in place You have worked inside at least two different business functions and understand their core workflows well enough to identify the next use case without being told The Director, AI Enablement trusts you to own the build layer independently - scoping conversations happen together, execution happens with you driving The Right Fit 2-4 years of experience that includes meaningful time working inside a business-facing function - operations, finance, marketing, customer success, HR, or similar - not just in Engineering or IT Hands-on experience building with AI tools: prompt engineering, automation platforms (Make, Zapier, n8n, or equivalent), API integrations, and at least working familiarity with RAG architectures and agent frameworks Proven ability to take a messy real-world process, understand it from the inside, and build something that makes it faster or better - not just technically cleaner Comfortable working with non-technical stakeholders: you can explain what you are building without jargon, gather requirements without a formal spec, and manage expectations when a prototype needs three more iterations Strong enough with code or no-code tools to get solutions to a deployable state independently - you do not need an engineer to ship your work Able to manage multiple active projects at different stages without dropping anything - a quick win in HR this week does not mean the Finance automation waits Genuinely curious about how companies work: the org chart, the incentives, the handoffs, the bottlenecks. This is what separates a good AI builder from a great one in a business context Bonus Points For Direct experience working in or closely with G&A, Finance, Legal, Marketing Ops, or Customer Success teams - you have lived in the workflows you will be redesigning Familiarity with AI governance basics: data handling, PII awareness, and when a use case needs a security or privacy review before it ships Experience working in a small program or startup environment where you wore multiple hats and shipped without a lot of process overhead Experience in cloud infrastructure, SaaS, or storage companies - comfort with technical products and the teams that build them A portfolio, GitHub, or examples of AI workflows or automations you have built - something you can show, not just describe At Backblaze, we value being fair and good to our customers, partners, and employees. AI-Native Engineering Experience Hands-on experience using AI development tools is especially important for this position. We're particularly interested in engineers who actively use tools such as: - Claude Code - OpenAI Codex - Cursor - Git Hub Copilot - Windsurf - Other AI coding agents or agentic development tools More importantly, we're looking for someone who uses AI beyond code completion. descripcion: The Opportunity We are seeking an experienced Senior Machine Learning Data Scientist to build fraud and abuse detection models and measure how effectively they work. Develop robust evaluation frameworks, datasets, and metrics to measure model and mitigation effectiveness. Design experiments and evaluate tradeoffs across precision, recall, customer impact, and fraud loss. Build dashboards and metrics that translate detection performance into measurable business impact. Partner across engineering, product, policy, and risk teams to turn insights into detection improvements and business decisions. What you'll need to succeed 8+ years in applied Data Science / ML, with experience building and evaluating production ML models. Strong foundation in statistical and classical ML, experimentation, model evaluation, and performance measurement. Strong hands-on Python and SQL skills working with large, complex datasets. Experience with model monitoring, drift, false-positive/false-negative analysis, and imperfect or delayed labels. Strong data visualization and storytelling skills — able to translate complex analysis into clear insights and recommendations. Strong analytical judgment, ownership, and ability to operate independently through ambiguity. Bachelor's or equivalent experience in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field; advanced degree a plus. Preferred Attributes Experience in fraud, abuse, risk, identity, trust & safety, or other adversarial domains. Experience with anomaly detection, clustering, behavioral modeling, or prevalence estimation. Experience with labeling frameworks, weak supervision, active learning, or human-review systems. Familiarity with LLMs and AI-assisted evaluation/analysis. Experience evaluating multi-layered risk controls and automated decisioning systems. About the role As a Lead Data Scientist for our Fraud team, you will be on the front lines of protecting our company and our customers. You will leverage your expertise in machine learning, statistics, and data analysis to design, build, and deploy sophisticated models that detect and prevent fraudulent activity in real-time. This is a high-impact role where you will see your work directly translate into protecting millions of dollars and ensuring a trustworthy platform for our users. Responsibilities Technical Leadership & Strategy: Define the long-term machine learning strategy for the fraud team, establish technical best practices, and mentor junior data scientists. End-to-End Model Development: Own the entire lifecycle of fraud detection models, from data exploration and feature engineering to model training, validation, deployment, and monitoring. Credit & Lending Fraud Mitigation: Design and develop models specifically targeted at lending fraud typologies, including synthetic identity fraud, first-party loan default fraud, and application fraud. Advanced Analysis: Conduct deep-dive investigations into emerging fraud patterns and user behavior, using clustering, outlier detection, network analysis, and other unsupervised techniques to uncover hidden risks and organized fraud rings. Experimentation: Design and execute A/B tests to measure the impact of new models, rules, and strategies on both fraud detection rates and user experience. Stakeholder Collaboration: Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, and Operations teams to translate business needs into data science solutions, seamlessly integrate ML scores with rule engines, and communicate complex results to non-technical audiences. Productionalize Models: Deploy, monitor, and maintain machine learning models in a cloud environment, ensuring high availability and performance. Reporting & Visualization: Build and maintain dashboards using tools like Tableau or Looker to track key performance indicators (KPIs) like fraud loss rates, false positive rates, and model performance. Requirements Must-Haves: Experience: 5+ years of experience in a hands-on data science role, building and deploying machine learning models. Leadership: Proven experience leading complex data science projects from inception to production, including setting technical direction and guiding peers. Python: Expert-level Python for data analysis and modeling (pandas, scikit-learn, etc.). SQL: Advanced SQL skills for complex data extraction and manipulation. Machine Learning Modeling: Deep experience with tree-based ML models (XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM) and statistical models (Logistic Regression, Lasso/Ridge). Model Explainability & Ethics: Deep understanding of model explainability frameworks (SHAP, LIME) and algorithmic fairness to ensure models comply with credit lending regulations. Sampling Techniques: Strong understanding of sampling techniques for handling highly imbalanced datasets. Unsupervised Learning: Practical experience with clustering and outlier detection techniques (e.g., K-Means, K Nearest Neighbors, Isolation Forest). Model Lifecycle & Cloud: Proven experience with the full modeling lifecycle, including model deployment, monitoring, and maintenance on a cloud platform like GCP, AWS, or Azure. Analytical Rigor: A solid foundation in statistics and experience designing and analyzing A/B tests. Communication: Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to explain complex technical concepts to diverse audiences. Advanced English level. Nice to have Domain Experience: Direct experience in a FinTech, payments, or risk/fraud-focused role, particularly with exposure to credit or consumer lending. Alternative & Bureau Data: Experience working with traditional credit bureau data (Experian, Equifax, TransUnion) and alternative credit/identity data sources. Graph ML: Experience with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) or graph analytics tools (e.g., Neo4j, NetworkX) to map complex fraud networks. Regulatory Familiarity: Familiarity with consumer lending regulations (e.g., FCRA, ECOA) and their impact on machine learning model development. MLOps: Hands-on MLOps experience (e.g., CI/CD for models, versioning, automated retraining). GCP / Vertex AI: Experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP), especially Vertex AI. These are the applicable requisites, although equivalent competencies in any of the above will also be considered. Implement inventory visibility tools and strategies to reduce obsolescence and working capital. Logistics And Distribution Support transportation, warehousing, and distribution operations to ensure timely and cost-effective product delivery to customers. Proactively manage risks related to supplier relationships, geopolitical factors, natural disasters, and other external threats.
